I am a woman of 42 years in the North East, and this millet plot is small, only about 0.36 hectares, so I must use what I have carefully. I intercrop my millet with cowpea like my mother taught me, because the soil here is tired and the rains are not always kind. I cannot read or write, and money for chemical fertilizer is hard to find, so I depend on the manure from my goats and the seeds I saved from last harvest. My children and I will do most of the work ourselves, but for weeding when the rains come heavy, I will call two or three people from the village to help for a few days.
